Subject: Private deployment: confirmation of EU hosting scope + SIG appendix

Hi Amanda / DataGuard team,

Following up on HealthBridge's private deployment request. They want final confirmation of the hosting scope and a compact SIG/CAIQ appendix we can hand to their procurement/security reviewers. Can you confirm the following items from Redwood's side so we can close the packet?

1) Canonical hosting region for the private deployment (customer-specified): eu-west-1 (Ireland) — please confirm node placement is limited to that region for prod pods.
2) VPC/private peering model: peering with HealthBridge VPC via PrivateLink (no public NAT for prod inference) — confirm egress policy and whether any control plane telemetry crosses out-of-region.
3) Keystore/KMS operations: where customer KMS keys will be held (Redwood-managed AWS KMS in eu-west-1, with optional BYOK via HSM) and whether operator access requires vaulted approvals.
4) SIG/CAIQ: we are attaching a condensed SIG subset for quick answers (redwood_sig_subset.csv) — we need a short appendix confirming any deviations from the SIG baseline (particularly around operator access, keystore operator roster, and cross-region backups).
5) SOC 2 artifacts: HealthBridge asked for a recent snapshot of relevant SOC 2 coverage for hosting and change control — we can provide a redacted snapshot if that helps.

Attachments: redwood_sig_subset.csv, private-deploy-checklist.pdf

Goal: assemble a one-page "hosting scope & exceptions" doc + the SIG appendix for their procurement folder by COB next Tue.

Thanks — copying Marissa for runbook/evidence handoff and Irene for compliance clarifications.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Enterprise 
Redwood Inference

Kimberly — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses from DataGuard's intake so we can route to HealthBridge's reviewers: 

- We can confirm HealthBridge prefers eu-west-1. Our intake flagged two items to confirm with your engineering/compliance teams: (A) if any backups or asynchronous replication targets exist in another region for DR, and (B) whether control-plane logs contain customer identifiers that transit through a US region.
- On SIG/CAIQ: the condensed CSV is helpful. We will accept a signed appendix that enumerates exceptions to the SIG baseline. The appendix should explicitly call out operator access controls and the sightlines you provide for keystore operator activities.
- SOC 2 slice: HealthBridge will accept a redacted SOC 2 snapshot limited to hosting/change-control sections.

Can you provide the appendix draft and the SOC 2 redacted PDF? Also please point us to any runbooks or network diagrams that show the PrivateLink peering flow and egress points (IP ranges, NAT behaviour).

Amanda Lewis

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment: confirmation of EU hosting scope + SIG appendix

Amanda — thanks, appreciate the checklist.

See the draft appendix and SOC 2 snapshot attached (redacted). Quick answers inline below and in the draft appendix: 

- Backups/DR: Production inference pods for HealthBridge will be pinned to eu-west-1. We maintain cross-region backups for metadata with encryption-at-rest but we do NOT replicate cold-model data outside eu-west-1 unless explicitly requested; that is a documented opt-in DR arrangement. This will be stated in the appendix.
- Control-plane logs: Control-plane telemetry (orchestration events) can be ingested in our control plane which may have aggregated endpoints in a US control plane for multi-region customers. We do NOT surface customer request/response payloads to that control plane. We will document the telemetry categories and retention.
- Operator access: Operator activities for private deployment are logged; keystore operator roster is available under NDA. We have two operational roles with least privilege: "privatelink-ops" and "keystore-admin"; the appendix will summarize role separation and approval workflow.

Related links (internal doc): https://drive.redwood.internal/privatedeploy/KB-482 (runbooks and network diagram). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deals/HB-2027-07-PRV-01

Attachments included: soc2-snapshot-2027-05.pdf (redacted), draft_sig_appendix_20270630.csv

I will loop Marissa to provide the peering IP ranges and the peering-runbook document.

Onward —
Kim

Hi Amanda / HealthBridge team — Marissa here from Platform Ops, providing the operational runbook pieces you requested.

Short answers and artifacts: 
- Peering & egress: PrivateLink peering terminates in the customer's VPC. Prod inference egress for outbound telemetry is restricted to our monitoring collector endpoint in eu-west-1 (no US egress by default). NAT is not used for customer request paths; egress used for model artifact downloads is served from eu-west-1 S3 endpoints.
- IP ranges: We hand over a /28 for the PrivateLink endpoint and the recommended BGP ranges in the runbook. See peering-runbook-privatelink_v2.docx for the exact CIDR recommendations and VPC endpoint setup steps.
- KMS / keystore: Customer-managed keys are supported via BYOK; Redwood-managed keys live in AWS KMS in eu-west-1 (region-restricted). Operator access to keystore operations uses short-lived IAM sessions with MFA + JIT approvals; all actions are logged to a tamper-evident audit store.
- Backups: metadata backup manifests are stored encrypted in eu-west-1. Cross-region backup is opt-in and will be explicitly documented and consented by HealthBridge.

Attachments we are providing in the packet: peering-runbook-privatelink_v2.docx, soc2-snapshot-2027-05.pdf (redacted), redwood_sig_subset.csv

Let me know if you need a signed appendix template (we can return a PDF with signatures) and if HealthBridge requires the keystore operator roster we will route that via NDA and a secure transfer.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Platform Operations Engineer
Redwood Inference
